channel.title: Topics on AI Security Atlas
channel.description: Recent content in Topics on AI Security Atlas

item.title: Activation steering
item.description: Change runtime representations using a chosen intervention and appropriate activation access.

item.title: Adaptive defense evaluation
item.description: Evaluate against an attacker who knows the defense rather than only stale fixed prompts.

item.title: Adversarial activation steering
item.description: Use runtime intervention to influence behavior without changing stored weights.

item.title: Adversarial fine-tuning to alter constraints
item.description: Use training control to modify a model’s refusal or other behavioral properties.

item.title: Adversarial input evasion
item.description: Perturb inputs or their presentation to change predictions or guardrail decisions.

item.title: Adversarial refusal-direction modification
item.description: Apply a refusal-related intervention to bypass a studied model constraint.

item.title: Adversarial training and robustness evaluation
item.description: Evaluate against an explicit perturbation set and adaptive attacks.

item.title: Agent authority and workflow attacks
item.description: Redirect tool use, memory or inter-agent workflows across trust boundaries.

item.title: Agent or connector confused-deputy abuse
item.description: Induce a more-privileged component to exercise authority for an unauthorized requester.

item.title: AgentDojo benchmark
item.description: A source-specific agent task and prompt-injection evaluation reference.

item.title: AI-assisted harmful activity
item.description: Use generation, analysis or automation for harmful purposes without necessarily breaking the model.

item.title: Appropriate model artifacts or capabilities
item.description: Acquire weights, adapters or functional imitation; separate exact artifact theft from behavioral replication.

item.title: Architectural applicability versus empirical evidence
item.description: A compatible surface is not an experimental demonstration of attack effectiveness.

item.title: Artifact, adapter or configuration substitution
item.description: Replace a trusted distribution object with an unreviewed version or misleading identity.

item.title: Attack success and severity
item.description: Define a measurable success event; distinguish model text from a consequential tool action.

item.title: Attack transferability
item.description: Success on one model or configuration does not establish success on a different target.

item.title: Attention and cross-attention
item.description: Attention mechanisms combine representations; cross-attention introduces distinct conditioning surfaces.

item.title: Auditable action and content lineage
item.description: Capture privacy-conscious provenance and tool decisions for investigation, not hidden reasoning extraction.

item.title: Authorization-aware retrieval
item.description: Filter by principal before disclosure and preserve access metadata through retrieval and generation.

item.title: Automated judge or grader manipulation
item.description: Influence grading instructions, context or feedback so a system appears more successful or safe.

item.title: Availability and cost attacks
item.description: Exploit resource allocation, input cost or uncontrolled loops.

item.title: Backdoor-oriented artifact evaluation
item.description: Test conditional behavior and clean utility; absence of a found trigger is not a proof of absence.

item.title: Behavioral tampering through merges or conversion
item.description: Introduce an untrusted component or update while transforming a model artifact.

item.title: Benchmark or evaluation contamination
item.description: Influence measurement by leaking evaluation material into training or changing the evaluation set.

item.title: Black-box functional model extraction
item.description: Train a substitute to imitate target behavior from queried outputs.

item.title: Browser and computer-use integrations
item.description: Rendered pages and document content can become model observations and trigger actions.

item.title: Cache and session isolation
item.description: Partition reusable state and measure information-sharing signals under realistic conditions.

item.title: Capability misuse
item.description: Use a legitimate model capability for harmful activity without assuming model compromise.

item.title: Cause unauthorized actions or privilege use
item.description: Redirect an agent or application into unauthorized tool calls, data access or changes.

item.title: Checkpoint conversion and sharding
item.description: Repackage representations and metadata; compatibility and integrity are separate questions.

item.title: Claim strength and verification depth
item.description: Separate theory, empirical reporting, independent reproduction, deployment reports and editorial hypotheses.

item.title: Classical predictive ML
item.description: Classifiers, regressors, trees and ensembles form an essential baseline beyond LLMs.

item.title: Classifier-free guidance
item.description: A generative guidance mechanism, not a safety-policy classifier.

item.title: Clean utility and false positives
item.description: Measure normal task completion and overblocking alongside attacks.

item.title: Compiled inference engines
item.description: Executable optimized plans, distinct from data-only weight containers.

item.title: Complete model package
item.description: Weights alone are insufficient: tokenizer, config, templates, revisions and auxiliary modules affect behavior.

item.title: Compromise the surrounding execution environment
item.description: Exploit loaders, packages, plugins, build systems or integrations to compromise the host or distribution channel.

item.title: Context windows and in-context learning
item.description: Information in the current context is different from information encoded in persistent weights.

item.title: Context-specific output validation
item.description: Treat generated code, markup and queries as untrusted input at their final sink.

item.title: Continued pretraining
item.description: Further training on a continued or domain-specific objective; not necessarily instruction tuning.

item.title: ControlNet-style conditioning
item.description: Add structured conditioning pathways to a generative pipeline.

item.title: Convolutional networks
item.description: Image-oriented convolutional architectures with spatial feature extraction.

item.title: Corpora, vector indexes and rerankers
item.description: Chunking, embeddings and ranking influence which external content reaches a model.

item.title: Cross-session or cross-tenant disclosure
item.description: Expose another principal’s data through state, context assembly, caching or access-control failures.

item.title: Data collection, filtering and deduplication
item.description: Dataset lineage and preprocessing affect privacy, integrity and evaluation reliability.

item.title: Dataset and artifact provenance
item.description: Record identities, immutable revisions, transformations and approval history.

item.title: Decoder-only autoregressive language models
item.description: Generate token sequences conditioned on preceding context; distinguish base and instruction-tuned checkpoints.

item.title: Degrade availability or increase cost
item.description: Exhaust capacity, latency, energy, tokens or tool budgets; distinguish algorithmic effects from generic request floods.

item.title: Deployment, monitoring and updates
item.description: Packaging, serving and integration change security exposure beyond the model checkpoint.

item.title: Differentially private training
item.description: Bound training contribution under a stated privacy definition and accounting procedure.

item.title: Diffusion and flow samplers
item.description: Inference schedules and solvers affect cost and outcomes independently of weights.

item.title: Diffusion backdoors / BadDiffusion
item.description: Alter training or diffusion processes to produce attacker-chosen outcomes under a trigger.

item.title: Diffusion generative models
item.description: Generative processes learned through noise-related denoising objectives, not a single backbone architecture.

item.title: Diffusion training-image extraction
item.description: Recover or closely reproduce training images under the conditions studied in extraction research.

item.title: Diffusion transformers
item.description: Transformer backbones used for diffusion; not equivalent to autoregressive language modeling.

item.title: Direct Preference Optimization
item.description: A preference-learning objective; distinguish standard DPO from reward-model-plus-PPO training.

item.title: Direct prompt injection
item.description: Attacker-supplied instructions attempt to override application task or trust policy.

item.title: DreamBooth personalization
item.description: Subject-specific diffusion fine-tuning; neutral personalization technique.

item.title: Embedding and reranking models
item.description: Representations and scoring models supporting retrieval and similarity workflows.

item.title: Encoder-decoder models
item.description: Separate source encoding and conditional sequence decoding.

item.title: Encoder-only language models
item.description: Bidirectional encoders used in representation learning and discriminative tasks.

item.title: Energy and latency amplification / sponge inputs
item.description: Construct expensive inputs for particular model and execution configurations.

item.title: Enforce authorization outside the model
item.description: Check the requesting principal, resource and action in deterministic application code.

item.title: Establish persistent attacker influence
item.description: Make attacker-selected behavior survive future sessions, triggers, updates or ordinary retraining.

item.title: Evade security controls or accountability
item.description: Defeat a deployed detector, monitoring or attribution control; metric-specific, not identical to refusal bypass.

item.title: Evaluation and accountability attacks
item.description: Distort measurement or evade a specific oversight control.

item.title: Evaluation data and benchmark governance
item.description: Separate training, attack development, validation and final testing.

item.title: Evaluation pipelines and automated judges
item.description: Judges, test sets and grading code are security-relevant dependencies.

item.title: Evasion of an ML security detector
item.description: Modify an input to avoid a specific classifier or deployed detector.

item.title: Evidence and citation laundering
item.description: Make untrustworthy content appear authoritative through generated references or retrieval chains.

item.title: Explicit threat model
item.description: State goals, capabilities, prior knowledge, budgets, authority and target revisions.

item.title: Exploitation of excessive delegated agency
item.description: Turn broadly granted tools or missing approvals into unauthorized actions.

item.title: Extraction fidelity versus artifact equality
item.description: Compare functional agreement, task quality and parameter recovery without conflating them.

item.title: Flow-matching generative models
item.description: Related continuous generative modeling objectives requiring their own objective and sampler labels.

item.title: Full-parameter fine-tuning
item.description: Update most or all model weights for a new objective; neutral adaptation.

item.title: Generative adversarial networks
item.description: Generator-discriminator training; the word adversarial here does not imply malicious use.

item.title: GGUF
item.description: Binary tensor/metadata packaging; can store different numerical types and supported architectures.

item.title: GPTQ
item.description: A specific post-training weight-quantization method, not a general model family.

item.title: Gradient-based adversarial perturbations / FGSM
item.description: Use input gradients to find perturbations that affect predictions.

item.title: Gradient-guided adversarial suffixes
item.description: Optimize discrete prompt suffixes through model or surrogate gradient information.

item.title: HarmBench benchmark
item.description: A source-specific red-team and robust refusal evaluation reference.

item.title: Hugging Face Diffusers
item.description: Composable generative pipelines and scheduler tooling.

item.title: Hugging Face Transformers
item.description: Model training/inference library; separate from transformer architecture.

item.title: Improper handling of model-generated output
item.description: A downstream application treats model output as executable or privileged input without appropriate validation.

item.title: Indirect prompt injection
item.description: Lower-trust documents or tool content carry instructions that an application treats as authority.

item.title: Inference engines and serving gateways
item.description: Batching, caches, request isolation and scheduling are runtime properties.

item.title: Input and output embeddings
item.description: Token or modality representations differ from a vector database entry and from output projection weights.

item.title: Instruction-tuning data poisoning
item.description: Corrupt demonstrations or labels used during supervised adaptation.

item.title: Instructions carried through multimodal content
item.description: Lower-trust visible text or interpreted media can become instructions in a multimodal workflow.

item.title: Inter-agent trust and message manipulation
item.description: Influence delegated workflows through messages treated as instructions or trusted results.

item.title: Iterative projected adversarial optimization
item.description: Evaluate robustness with iterative constrained perturbation search.

item.title: Jailbreaking and refusal bypass
item.description: Elicit behavior outside an operator’s intended model behavior constraints.

item.title: Knowledge distillation
item.description: Teacher-student transfer can be authorized development or support unauthorized functional imitation.

item.title: KV caches and prefix reuse
item.description: Inference-state caching can create isolation and timing considerations depending on implementation.

item.title: Language-model training-data extraction
item.description: Recover training-specific text through model interaction in a setting that permits verification.

item.title: Latent diffusion pipelines
item.description: Diffusion operates in a learned latent space, with separate encoding and decoding components.

item.title: Latent spaces and codecs
item.description: Latent representations, encoders and decoders contribute separate generative-system surfaces.

item.title: Least-privilege contribution and CI pipeline
item.description: Separate untrusted content inspection from credentials, deployment and executable builds.

item.title: Least-privilege tools and scoped credentials
item.description: Limit reachable actions and data; approval must bind to actual arguments and destinations.

item.title: llama.cpp
item.description: Inference runtime commonly associated with GGUF artifacts.

item.title: Logits, probabilities and observable outputs
item.description: API output granularity changes what an attacker can infer or optimize.

item.title: LoRA
item.description: Train low-rank update matrices; malicious behavior depends on data, objective and deployment.

item.title: Losses, gradients and optimization
item.description: Training signals and their visibility matter for optimization attacks and privacy leakage.

item.title: Machine unlearning and concept erasure
item.description: Attempts to remove learned influence or concepts require explicit success definitions and adversarial evaluation.

item.title: Malicious adapters or adapter substitution
item.description: Distribute or apply an attacker-controlled adaptation artifact to alter behavior.

item.title: Malicious dependencies or repository code
item.description: Compromise the application through imported code, plugins or build dependencies.

item.title: Manipulate outputs, predictions or decisions
item.description: Change a task result, ranking, generated artifact or downstream decision in the attacker’s favor.

item.title: Many-shot context attacks
item.description: Use long sequences of demonstrations to steer behavior in the studied long-context setting.

item.title: Membership inference
item.description: Estimate whether a candidate record was included in a model’s training set.

item.title: Memorization, generalization and duplication
item.description: Retaining training-specific information is distinct from merely learning a distribution.

item.title: Memory provenance, review and expiry
item.description: Record who introduced persistent state and allow scoped review, revocation and reset.

item.title: Mixture-of-experts models
item.description: Sparse expert routing is a component choice that can coexist with transformer backbones.

item.title: MLX
item.description: Array and ML framework often used in Apple-silicon environments.

item.title: Model and adapter merging
item.description: Combine compatible parameters or updates; provenance and behavioral regressions must be reassessed.

item.title: Model artifact theft and functional extraction
item.description: Acquire artifacts or reproduce behavior with distinct threat models.

item.title: Model inversion and attribute inference
item.description: Infer sensitive attributes or input-related information from model behavior and auxiliary knowledge.

item.title: Model loaders and executable repository code
item.description: Parsing or importing model artifacts is a separate host-execution trust decision.

item.title: Model registries and distribution
item.description: Artifacts, revisions, licenses and upstream dependencies need provenance.

item.title: Multi-agent orchestration
item.description: Messages and delegated authority cross multiple component boundaries.

item.title: Neural networks
item.description: Parameterized differentiable models; a shared prerequisite, not a specific generative family.

item.title: Noise schedules and denoising objectives
item.description: Noise parameterization and time steps distinguish diffusion-specific interventions.

item.title: Obtain protected information
item.description: Infer or disclose training examples, attributes, prompts, retrieved records, session data or secrets without authorization.

item.title: ONNX
item.description: Interchange representation with computational graphs, operators and parameters.

item.title: Optimized visual jailbreaks
item.description: Use adversarial visual perturbations to affect a vision-language model’s safety behavior.

item.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
item.description: Adapt a subset or added parameters rather than all model weights.

item.title: Partial parameter recovery from API behavior
item.description: Recover a model projection component or dimensions under specific query and score assumptions.

item.title: Persistent agent memory
item.description: Stored summaries, preferences or instructions can influence later sessions.

item.title: Persistent agent-memory poisoning
item.description: Plant or induce stored entries that redirect future tasks or decisions.

item.title: Persistent conditional LLM backdoors
item.description: Study intentionally implanted conditional behavior that can survive tested safety-training procedures.

item.title: Physical-world adversarial examples
item.description: Study perturbations after printing, capture or other real-world transformations.

item.title: Poisoning, backdoors and persistence
item.description: Corrupt inputs to learning or persistent state to influence later behavior.

item.title: Post-training
item.description: Umbrella for adaptation after pretraining, including but not limited to alignment.

item.title: Preference data and reward models
item.description: Human or synthetic comparisons can influence post-training objectives.

item.title: Preference or reward-signal manipulation
item.description: Influence comparisons, reward models or feedback used in post-training.

item.title: Prefix tuning
item.description: Learn continuous prefixes while freezing base parameters.

item.title: Pretraining
item.description: Initial broad learning from a training objective and corpus.

item.title: Pretraining data poisoning
item.description: Influence learned behavior by contributing or changing data before broad training.

item.title: Privacy inference and data extraction
item.description: Infer or reconstruct protected data under different visibility assumptions.

item.title: Privacy verification and baselines
item.description: Use membership baselines, record verification, confidence and task-appropriate similarity criteria.

item.title: Prompt and context manipulation
item.description: Attacks that reinterpret or override instructions through model-visible inputs.

item.title: Prompt-cache timing inference
item.description: Use observable service timing to investigate shared caching or prior prompt use.

item.title: Pruning and sparsity
item.description: Remove or constrain parameters/connections; security effects are not guaranteed by compression.

item.title: PyTorch checkpoints and pickle-related loading
item.description: Checkpoint extensions do not fully describe loading behavior or executable deserialization risk.

item.title: QLoRA
item.description: Combine quantized base weights with low-rank adaptation; neither a model format nor an attack.

item.title: Quantization and numerical precision
item.description: Change numerical representation, often with calibration; separate from serialization and training stage.

item.title: Query, token, latency and compute cost
item.description: Report budgets and resource impact with the exact experimental configuration.

item.title: RAG knowledge-base poisoning
item.description: Insert or modify retrieved evidence to steer generated answers or decisions.

item.title: Reconstruction from gradients or updates
item.description: Recover information about training inputs from exposed gradients or model updates.

item.title: Refusal-direction ablation / abliteration
item.description: Refusal-related interventions may use activation ablation or derived weight edits; narrower than removing every safeguard.

item.title: Representation and weight interventions
item.description: White-box model modifications and runtime interventions applied adversarially.

item.title: Representation engineering
item.description: Analyze or modify internal representations; neutral methodological umbrella.

item.title: Reproducibility and statistical uncertainty
item.description: Store seeds, versions, sampling rules, test split and confidence intervals where meaningful.

item.title: Request, token, tool and cost budgets
item.description: Enforce per-principal limits and wall-clock or recursion boundaries outside model discretion.

item.title: Residual streams and block structure
item.description: Shared representation pathways are relevant to localized activation and weight interventions.

item.title: Responsible disclosure and safe research
item.description: Use authorized test environments, minimize sensitive data, and preserve correction and retraction workflows.

item.title: Retrieval and knowledge manipulation
item.description: Influence external evidence, selection, authorization or attribution.

item.title: Retrieval and ranking manipulation
item.description: Influence which attacker-controlled material is selected as evidence.

item.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
item.description: Retrieval, ranking, authorization, prompt assembly and generation are separate components.

item.title: Risk-based human approval
item.description: Require informed approval for high-impact actions without presenting approval as a universal protection.

item.title: RLHF and policy optimization
item.description: Learning from feedback may involve a reward model and policy optimization; not the only alignment route.

item.title: Safer tensor loading and dependency control
item.description: Prefer constrained serialization and audited loaders while retaining parser and behavioral checks.

item.title: Safetensors
item.description: Tensor serialization with a safer loading design; does not establish benign learned behavior.

item.title: Safety and instruction tuning
item.description: Intended behavioral constraints are learned properties that need evaluation after modifications.

item.title: Safety and utility regression testing
item.description: Reevaluate changed checkpoints, adapters, merges and configurations on held-out tests.

item.title: Sampling and decoding configuration
item.description: Temperature, selection rules and stopping conditions affect generated outputs without retraining.

item.title: Sandboxing, egress and execution isolation
item.description: Limit what compromised model-adjacent code or agents can execute and reach.

item.title: Separate data from authority
item.description: Keep lower-trust content from granting itself privileges; defense in depth, not a perfect prompt-only filter.

item.title: Soft prompt tuning
item.description: Learn prompt embeddings rather than authoring ordinary discrete text prompts.

item.title: State-space and hybrid sequence models
item.description: Alternative or hybrid sequence computation; transformer-specific edits do not transfer automatically.

item.title: Supervised fine-tuning
item.description: Optimize on labeled demonstrations or input-output examples.

item.title: Supply-chain and runtime compromise
item.description: Compromise loaders, artifacts, dependencies or hosting components.

item.title: System or developer prompt disclosure
item.description: Attempt to disclose hidden configuration text supplied to the model.

item.title: Targeted model editing
item.description: Modify selected learned associations; locality and side effects require evaluation.

item.title: TensorRT / TensorRT-adjacent serving
item.description: Optimization and execution ecosystem requiring explicit engine and plugin trust.

item.title: Text, image and control conditioning
item.description: Conditioning can enter through text encoders, cross-attention or additional control branches.

item.title: Textual inversion
item.description: Learned concept embeddings for generation; not the same concept as privacy model inversion.

item.title: Token, context and inference-budget exhaustion
item.description: Cause excessive permitted work through input/output length or uncontrolled request behavior.

item.title: Tokenization and vocabulary
item.description: Text segmentation and special tokens are part of the model input contract.

item.title: Tool definition or behavior changes after approval
item.description: Change a tool after it has acquired user or client trust.

item.title: Tool-description poisoning
item.description: Influence tool selection or actions through attacker-controlled tool metadata.

item.title: Tool-loop and recursive-delegation exhaustion
item.description: Induce repeated actions or delegated calls when agent execution lacks effective budgets.

item.title: Tool-output injection
item.description: Return lower-trust instructions in a tool response to redirect an agent.

item.title: Tool-using agents
item.description: A loop combines model decisions, tools, observations and policy enforcement.

item.title: Tools, plugins, MCP and connectors
item.description: Descriptions, arguments, outputs, identity and authorization are distinct tool surfaces.

item.title: Training and adaptation abuse
item.description: Attacker-influenced data, objectives or updates can change model behavior.

item.title: Training-data minimization and deduplication
item.description: Reduce unnecessary sensitive or repeated records; does not provide a formal privacy guarantee.

item.title: Transfer and architecture boundaries
item.description: Distinguish source-model success, target-model transfer, adaptation and unsupported generalization.

item.title: Transfer of adversarial prompts
item.description: Apply an attack constructed on a source model to a different target.

item.title: Transformers
item.description: Attention-based blocks used in multiple modeling objectives and modalities.

item.title: Trigger-conditioned model backdoors
item.description: Implant attacker-selected behavior activated by a trigger while retaining ordinary utility.

item.title: Trust boundaries and authorization
item.description: Track where data, instructions and authority cross from one principal or component to another.

item.title: U-Net-style diffusion backbones
item.description: Convolutional multiscale denoisers often used within image diffusion pipelines.

item.title: Unauthorized checkpoint or adapter theft
item.description: Acquire exact artifacts through storage, account or supply-chain compromise.

item.title: Unauthorized factual model editing
item.description: Modify selected model associations to influence later answers.

item.title: Unauthorized retrieved-document disclosure
item.description: Reveal content the requesting principal should not be authorized to retrieve or view.

item.title: Unauthorized teacher-student capability transfer
item.description: Apply distillation or imitation to acquire capabilities without required permission.

item.title: Unsafe checkpoint deserialization
item.description: A loader executes or interprets malicious artifact content during model loading.

item.title: Unsloth
item.description: Efficiency-oriented model tooling; not pretraining, post-training, architecture or file format.

item.title: Use AI to amplify harmful activity
item.description: Adjacent misuse lens: abuse a capability without necessarily compromising the model or its host.

item.title: Variational autoencoders
item.description: Latent-variable encoders and decoders; can also be components of larger generative pipelines.

item.title: Violate intended behavioral constraints
item.description: Cause the system to produce behavior its operator intends to disallow; includes safeguard bypass but not all output errors.

item.title: Vision-language models
item.description: Coupled visual representations and language processing introduce multiple input pathways.

item.title: vLLM
item.description: Serving runtime with version-dependent scheduling and caching behavior.

item.title: Weights, parameters and activations
item.description: Distinguish persistent learned tensors from input-dependent intermediate activations.
